prompt: Assemble the argument list for a "java" command line, then render it as a quoted string. Complete both JavaCommandBuilder methods and run the tests.
explanation: A command line is an ordered list of tokens, and the order is part of the contract: JVM options must come before the main class, program arguments after it. Copying the property map into a TreeMap gives the -D options a stable, sorted order no matter how the caller built the map. Validating mainClass up front with IllegalArgumentException fails fast instead of producing a command that cannot run.
hints: Build an ArrayList<String> and add tokens in the documented order; return it at the end.
new TreeMap<>(systemProperties) gives you the same entries sorted by key, which is all the sorting you need.
Check mainClass first and throw IllegalArgumentException before adding anything, and remember a blank string is not a valid class name.
